title: Student Affairs ChatBot
subtitle: LLaMA-Based AI Chatbot for University Student Services — Graduation Project
description: An AI-powered chatbot developed as a graduation project at Kırıkkale University that answers frequently asked student affairs questions with 92% accuracy. Built on the LLaMA architecture with fine-tuning, web scraping for data collection, and three data augmentation techniques to overcome limited training data.
longDescription:
Student Affairs ChatBot is an AI assistant developed to solve a real problem in university environments: student affairs offices receive the same repetitive questions every semester, overloading staff and slowing down students' access to information.

The system was built on the LLaMA large language model architecture, fine-tuned using the Face FungE method on a custom dataset collected from Kırıkkale University's official student affairs web pages via web scraping. Since the collected data was limited in volume, three data augmentation techniques were applied to enrich the training set: EDA (Easy Data Augmentation) for word-level variations, Back-Translation for natural paraphrasing through translation, and T5-based paraphrasing for semantic rewriting.

The result is a chatbot that understands natural language questions from students and responds with accurate, context-appropriate answers — 24/7, without staff intervention. In user testing, the system achieved a 92% correct response rate.

The project was developed as a graduation project at Kırıkkale University, Computer Engineering Department, under the supervision of Assoc. Prof. Dr. Fahrettin HORASAN, in collaboration with team member Yusuf Ömer KARA. It was presented at the 2024–2025 Graduation Projects Exhibition.

contentBlocks.heading: Project Overview
contentBlocks.subheading: A 24/7 AI Assistant for University Student Services
contentBlocks.content:
Student Affairs ChatBot was developed to address a real and persistent problem in university environments: student affairs offices receive the same repetitive questions every semester — about course registration, exam schedules, deadlines, library hours, and more. This overloads staff and slows down students who need quick answers.

The chatbot provides accurate, natural-language answers to these questions around the clock, without any staff involvement. Students simply type their question in Turkish and receive an immediate, contextually appropriate response.

The system was developed as a graduation project at Kırıkkale University, Computer Engineering Department, under the supervision of **Assoc. Prof. Dr. Fahrettin HORASAN**, in collaboration with **Yusuf Ömer KARA**. It was presented at the **2024–2025 Graduation Projects Exhibition**.

contentBlocks.heading: Motivation
contentBlocks.subheading: Why this problem needed a smart solution
contentBlocks.content:
**Repetitive Information Requests**
Questions directed to student affairs offices are highly repetitive by nature. The same questions about registration, exams, and deadlines are asked hundreds of times each semester by different students. This project automates responses to these queries with an accessible, user-friendly chatbot.

**Human-Like Responses via NLP**
The model is built on the LLaMA architecture and trained to understand questions posed in natural Turkish language — going beyond traditional keyword-based retrieval systems to provide intuitive, human-like answers.

**Strengthening Deep Learning with Data Augmentation**
To overcome limited training data availability, EDA, Back-Translation, and T5-based paraphrasing were used to enrich the dataset, improving the model's ability to handle diverse phrasings of the same question.

**A Novel Use Case: Smart Interface for Institutional Knowledge**
Most chatbot applications target commercial domains. This project presents an original application that combines institutional knowledge access with a modern conversational interface in a university environment.

contentBlocks.heading: System Pipeline
contentBlocks.subheading: From raw web data to a fine-tuned conversational model
contentBlocks.content:
**Step 1 — Data Collection (Web Scraping)**
Training data was collected from Kırıkkale University's official student affairs web pages using Python's BeautifulSoup and Requests libraries. The scraping process systematically extracted structured Q&A content from the institutional website.

**Step 2 — Data Augmentation**
Since the collected dataset was limited in size, three augmentation techniques were applied to expand and diversify the training data:

- **EDA (Easy Data Augmentation)** — Word deletion and synonym substitution to create natural sentence variations
- **Back-Translation** — Sentences translated to a foreign language and back to Turkish, generating naturally paraphrased versions
- **T5 Paraphrasing** — Google's T5 model used to rewrite sentences semantically while preserving their meaning

**Step 3 — Model Fine-tuning**
The LLaMA architecture was selected as the base model. Fine-tuning was performed using the **Face FungE** method on the augmented dataset, structured in a question-answer format. The model was optimized to produce correct responses to the types of questions students ask.

**Step 4 — Deployment & Testing**
The chatbot was deployed with a chat interface and evaluated through user testing, achieving a **92% correct response rate**.

contentBlocks.heading: Results & Discussion
contentBlocks.content:
The system demonstrated strong performance in answering the most frequently asked student affairs questions with high accuracy and speed.

**Key findings from user testing:**
- The chatbot provided correct information in **92% of test cases**
- The LLaMA architecture provided a strong foundation for Turkish natural language understanding
- Data augmentation successfully overcame the limited dataset challenge, improving the model's tolerance to varied phrasings
- The Q&A training format was effectively learned by the model

**Limitations & Future Work:**
The model currently relies on a static dataset. For the system to stay current with institutional changes (new policies, updated schedules), a dynamic data pipeline — such as an API integration with the university's information system — is recommended.

Future development targets include multi-language support, mobile platform integration, and a self-updating architecture driven by user feedback.

contentBlocks.heading: Future Roadmap
contentBlocks.content:
- **Multi-language support** — Extend the chatbot to answer in Arabic and English in addition to Turkish
- **Mobile integration** — Deploy the chatbot as a native mobile application
- **Continuous learning** — Implement a feedback loop where user interactions improve the model over time
- **API integration** — Connect to the university's live information systems for real-time data updates
- **Expanded coverage** — Extend beyond student affairs to cover library, cafeteria, dormitory, and academic calendar queries
